Hi James / Sarah — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side after the demo: 

Call recap (high level):
- Use case: customer-facing analytics assistant that summarizes reports and answers follow-ups over user-provided data.
- Model family: planning to run a 70B-class open model (PF-style quantized) in a low-latency, high-throughput setup.
- Average sequence length: ~256 tokens (95% under 512).
- Expected concurrency: baseline 10-20 concurrent requests, peak bursts to 40 concurrent.

Key items we agreed to follow up on:
1) Confirm monthly token volume range you expect (helpful for unit economics).
2) Share target $ per 1M tokens or budget range for dedicated capacity.
3) Preferred GPU (A100 80GB vs H100) and whether you need latest-gen for latency.
4) Throughput targets / SLOs (p95 latency targets, tokens/sec).

From our side — preliminary guidance (subject to Marcus' throughput sizing):
- Typical dedicated reserved capacity for this workload ranges from 2x H100 (entry) to 4x H100 (production) or 4-8x A100 80GB depending on model ops and batching.
- Ballpark unit economics: at ~50-200M tokens/month, customers see effective pricing in the ~$600–$1,000 per 1M-token range on dedicated plans (varies with utilization and batching).

Please reply with the answers to items 1-3 and we'll have Marcus run a short throughput/slot recommendation and a formal pricing sheet. I attached a first-pass pricing PDF and a small spreadsheet for you to drop in expected volumes.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scoped out.

Marissa — thanks for the summary. A few quick answers from our side: 

1) Estimated token volume: we expect 100M-300M tokens/month in the first 6 months, with growth to ~600M/month within 12-18 months if the pilot succeeds. Those are user-generated tokens (prompt+response).
2) Budget: for production dedicated infra we're thinking $30k–$80k/month committed. For pilot we can do a smaller reserved commit + burst.
3) GPU preference: we prefer H100 for latency-critical inference; happy to discuss A100 if the cost delta is significant.
4) Throughput/SLO: target p95 completion latency <= 2s for responses of ~256 tokens; peak concurrency 40.

I've attached the rough traffic profile (see acme-throughput-estimates.xlsx) — hope this helps. Can Marcus size an initial config (2x H100? 4x A100?) and give rough $/1M tokens estimates at both pilot and scaled volumes?

Thanks James — good details. I ran a quick back-of-envelope sizing based on the numbers you sent and common model characteristics for a quantized 70B: 

Assumptions: average seq len = 256 tokens, model is 4-bit quantized, we target aggressive batching but want bounded latency for p95 <= 2s.

Sizing guidance (rough):
- Pilot / low commit (100M tokens/month): 2x H100 (or 4x A100 80GB) as a reserved pool should cover baseline with headroom for bursts if we allow autoscaling/burst pools. Expected sustained throughput ~80-150k tokens/min per H100 depending on batching; per-cluster throughput scales linearly.
- Production (300-600M tokens/month): 4x H100 recommended or 8x A100. This delivers steady-state throughput for your concurrency target with ~20-30% headroom for spikes.

Unit economics (indicative):
- At 100M tokens/mo: effective cost ~ $900–$1,200 per 1M tokens (lower utilization during pilot increases unit cost).
- At 300-600M tokens/mo: effective cost ~ $600–$850 per 1M tokens (higher utilization + batching improvements).

Notes: H100 gives a ~1.5-2x latency/throughput improvement vs A100 for the models we benchmark; cost delta will vary by vendor/region. If Acme can accept slightly higher p95, we can push more batching and get better $/1M economics on A100s.

Next steps from me: I can produce a short table with 2x/4x H100 and 4x/8x A100 options that lists estimated monthly cost, expected tokens/month capacity, and rough $/1M tokens. Want me to put that in a one-pager and update the attached pricing PDF?

—Marcus
